preamble: Reduction of the close back vowel [u] to schwa [ə] in unstressed syllables, with loss of rounding and height. In the transition from late Old English to Early Middle English all unstressed vowels, including final -u, merged into a vowel written e, which probably represented /ə/; the final schwa was itself lost by Chaucer's time in normal speech.

examples.note: Unstressed final -u was reduced to /ə/, written e; it was later lost (modern son).
The stressed vowel was also lengthened and lowered by open-syllable lengthening.
